claims.text: The Co-free alloy has an equiatomic Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn composition.
The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a conventionally processed solid solution.
FeNiCrMn is derived by removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi contains 20 at.% each of Co, Cr, Fe, Mn, and Ni.
The Cantor alloy commonly forms a chemically disordered FCC solid solution over a wide temperature range below its solidus.
The Cantor alloy's improved strength-ductility combination at decreasing temperature is closely related to deformation-induced nanotwins and stacking faults.
The dynamic strength-ductility balance of Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by a temperature- and strain-rate-dependent transition in the dominant plastic-deformation mechanism.
Removing Co changes stacking-fault energy and local atomic interactions.
At lower temperatures or higher strain rates, removing Co suppresses deformation twinning relative to the Cantor alloy.
Under lower-temperature or higher-strain-rate conditions, Co-free FeNiCrMn deforms predominantly by dislocation glide.
Suppressed twinning and dislocation-dominated deformation produce greater stored strain energy and earlier dynamic recrystallization.
At higher temperatures or lower strain rates, thermally activated dislocation climb and recovery dominate deformation in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Dislocation climb and recovery reduce flow stress while preserving ductility.
Under matched low-temperature and high-strain-rate conditions, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have a statistically significantly lower twin density than CoCrFeMnNi.
Co-free FeNiCrMn will exhibit earlier dynamic-recrystallization onset than CoCrFeMnNi at elevated temperatures or lower strain rates.
Co-free FeNiCrMn will exhibit a distinct stress-strain response and altered work-hardening exponents relative to CoCrFeMnNi.

The proposed mechanism applies from cryogenic temperatures to approximately 600 degrees Celsius while the Co-free alloy remains a single-phase solid solution without precipitation or phase separation.
The proposed mechanism applies at moderate to high strain rates.

contradictions.description: The mechanistic narrative assigns earlier dynamic recrystallization to lower-temperature or higher-strain-rate deformation, whereas the explicit comparative prediction assigns earlier recrystallization to elevated temperatures or lower strain rates. The intended regime for this prediction is therefore internally inconsistent.
The conditions include rates ranging from high to low, but the stated applicability boundary restricts the hypothesis to moderate-to-high strain rates.
